page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v5 is an enterprise general-purpose instance powered by the 3rd Gen AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It includes 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by standard hardware encryption extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance scored within the top 25 percent in stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU evaluation, and Geekbench multi-core assessments. Memory performance is particularly competitive, placing in the top 10 percent of the PassMark memory benchmark with small-block cached read bandwidth reaching 3114.99 GB/sec. Cryptographic handling and multi-threaded decompression also place in the upper quartile. Conversely, tasks that rely heavily on single-thread clock speed or advanced vector operations absent from this configuration, such as AVX-512, yield average results.

The D48as_v5 does not bundle local disk storage or include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Storage throughput and persistence require the configuration of external Azure managed disks such as Premium Storage. Because there is no local storage, storage performance is strictly dictated by attached network-based block volumes.

This server type is suitable for scale-up multi-threaded applications, enterprise web backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and memory-sensitive relational or in-memory databases. It is less suited for heavy deep-learning model generation, where tests on large language models revealed significant processing bottlenecks due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure D48as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. Utilizing a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio across 24 physical cores with hyperthreading, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU and memory subsystem benchmarks, including strong scores in PassMark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded decompression tests. The instance includes no bundled local storage and requires remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent file and disk management. Without discrete GPU accelerators or AVX-512 instruction support, it is not engineered for deep learning model training. Instead, the hardware configuration provides balanced resource density and reliable execution suited for multi-threaded enterprise services, memory-heavy database operations, and continuous integration compilation workloads.
